names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 4 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Πετρόκιος ο εξ Ουαλίας», with the rank words left off.

birth.note: saint.gr's head line reads «Οσιος Πετροκιος ο Εξ Ουαλιας (468 - 564)» and the entry says he was born in 468 in southern Wales.

death.note: saint.gr says he fell asleep in peace in 564, that he was buried at Padstow and that his relics were moved to the church at Bodmin.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Πετρόκιος ο εξ Ουαλίας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and does not carry the «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. saint.gr's head line dates him «(468 - 564)» and the entry names many places: southern Wales, Ireland, Hailesmouth, Lanwethinoc — later Petrockstow and now Padstow — Rome, the Holy Land, an island in the Indian Ocean, Petherick and Bodmin. `locations` is left out for that reason and not for want of detail. The page hedges his parentage: younger son, or by others' account nephew, of Saint Claudius Kerniv, king of Glywysing, whom it dates to 3 May; it also names Saint Goran, 7 April. Neither day was opened for this draft, so the life names both men without a link and there is no `related` row. The day's line calls him the protector of Cornwall. The corpus keeps nobody of this name. No hymn is printed.
